reviews.text: Found a leaflet in a pub toilet in Hull for this game. Great game! Simple but addictive game play loop. Lesson learnt to pay more attention to all adverts in the mens loo's!

The game itself is enjoyable once you get past the very first bit where you have very few tools and options. Unfortunately, the base gameplay loop is overshadowed by a storyline where you are punished, punished, punished. More debt, more interest, if anything happens that's a benefit to you it's actually a trap and you'll just be punished more. This makes it not fun by itself but, the threat is there for the story. You can "get out" of your debt with hidden messages giving you instructions, first to destroy some drones in the next mission (clearly labeled, i did that), then another telling you to destroy a scrap machine with red crystals before a set date. Then no mission was available to me that had both a scrap machine and red crystal at any of the following missions, so on that date i got the message "Understood. You do not want our help"... So the storyline in this relatively story-centric game basically got disabled by the game's own RNG. I would need to start over and play another three hours to get back to where i was.
Overall miserable experience.
Once I pay off my debt the company will recognize what a valuable asset I am.

Trap corpos in the space. Stomp corpo skulls with a big ship. Drown corpos in fried red crystal grease. Vaporize corpos with gatling gun. Nuke corpos.

A fun little mining game Progression feels really well with almost each unlocked upgrade feeling like a significant increase of QoL The game suffers slightly from being a bit too tedius at times. It also does lack variety in gameplay department. The lowest hanging fruits would be an endless mode after the main campaign, moving asteroid belts where the inertia switch is very beneficial. Or just plain more things to dig up, imagine bigger gems with weird shapes to free from asteroid grasp etc The cliche anti capitalism messaging is strong, but not obnoxious

A fun short space mining game, I really like how the game does a good job of exploring it's set of mechanics, and there are a few creative mining techniques with the physics that you can figure out for yourself.

A great little time waster. I honestly expected to skip all the story bits, but I ended up getting hooked. The way it's told is surprisingly engaging, and the setting does a great job of keeping things interesting. The controls and movement feel really good. Everything is smooth and responsive, which makes the gameplay satisfying from start to finish. I do wish there was a bit more content, but considering the price, it's absolutely worth it, especially if you can pick it up on sale. If the game looks interesting to you, I'd definitely say it's worth giving it a shot.

A simple yet extremely engrossing asteroid mining game, with a suite of mining tools and explosives as well as mission hazards that interact with the game's physics system, and hypnotically good OST.
Navigate zero-g asteroid fields, mine with real-time physics, and battle a cold corporation in a pixel-art 2D space-mining sim where every crash, burn and upgrade counts in your bid to survive.
Every asteroid you shred, every rock you chip away tells a story of imbalance and corporate greed. The mix of retro visuals and harsh survival touches elevates the mining sim genre.
🚀 Deep Space Exploitation - Addictive space mining with gritty pixel charm! Upgrading ships, smashing asteroids and defying greedy corps feels thrilling and tense. A cosmic grind done right 🌌⚒️
Deep Space Exploitation is a 2D pixel space mining game. Upgrade your ship, master physics-driven asteroids, and make tough choices to survive exploitative corporations and secure your future.
What a delight. Fun gameplay, funny writing, charming early 90s graphics, tight controls, delightful music. I don't have a bad thing to say about it.

Deep Space Exploitation is a tense space-mining game with 2D physics, destructible asteroids and a ruthless corporate backdrop. Upgrade wisely. Achievements.
Fun loop but the corp breathing down your neck gives every haul real bite. Rocks pop nice, upgrades feel earned, and the whole vibe is gritty in a good way.

You pilot a space mining ship in a brutal future, smashing asteroids to smithereens using true 2D physics. Resource gathering is intense, explosions feel powerful, and corporate greed knows no bounds.
Deep Space Exploitation excels as a resource management and action sim, where every choice matters, crafting a tense, rewarding space survival experience in a beautiful pixel-art coat.
Deep Space Exploitation — атмосферный sci-fi рогалайт, где вы исследуете заброшенные станции, управляете ресурсами и сражаетесь с аномалиями. Интенсивный геймплей держит в напряжении.
🎮 GAMEPLAY: 7/10 | 🎨 GRAPHICS: 5/10 | 🔊 AUDIO: 7/10 | 📚 STORY: 5/10 | A pixel art aesthetic and clear survival narrative enhance the atmosphere as you manage risks vs rewards. A thoughtful mix!
